title: Pea protein
description: Lead, cadmium, mercury and arsenic evidence for pea protein isolate and concentrate, with labeled-serving arithmetic, applicable limits and what a buyer should ask a supplier.
lede: Two retail pea protein powders carry the only published single-product metal results for pea protein: both contained lead and cadmium, and neither was tested for arsenic.

answers.text: Lead and cadmium are the supported concerns: both were present in the two pea protein powders measured, and mercury was quantified in one of them. Arsenic is unassessed because it was not measured.

citation_spans.after: Lead and cadmium are the supported concerns: both were present in the two pea protein powders measured, and mercury was quantified in one of them.
Arsenic is unassessed because it was not measured.

answers.text: Lot testing for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic deserves priority, because the two measured powders differed by more than twofold in cadmium at nearly equal lead. Origin-based sourcing cannot be prioritized on current evidence.

citation_spans.after: Lot testing for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic deserves priority, because the two measured powders differed by more than twofold in cadmium at nearly equal lead.

presentation.text: Two retail pea protein powders, bought in Ireland in 2016 and 2017, are the only pea protein products in the Index with published single-product metal results. Both carried lead, at 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg, and cadmium, at 40.6 and 15.4 µg/kg; mercury was 4.3 µg/kg in one and below the 0.2 µg/kg quantification limit in the other. Arsenic was not measured.

citation_spans.after: Two retail pea protein powders, bought in Ireland in 2016 and 2017, are the only pea protein products in the Index with published single-product metal results.
Both carried lead, at 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg, and cadmium, at 40.6 and 15.4 µg/kg; mercury was 4.3 µg/kg in one and below the 0.2 µg/kg quantification limit in the other.
Arsenic was not measured.
